compose verb

also write (a poem, a letter, a piece), compose music, composition, put together, compile

classical

Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.4: poēma (Lewis & Short)
Hor. S. 1.4.8: versūs (Lewis & Short)
Tib. 1.2.53: cantūs (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 294

compōnō, compōnere, composuī, compositum

verb, third conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

compose, write (a book, a poem, a letter)

To put a written work together: books, speeches, letters, edicts, verses. Its first sense is “put together, arrange”, and it also means settle a quarrel and lay out the dead.

Other words

  • faciō, facere, fēcī, factum — make (verses, a poem)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Pis. 70: poēma (Lewis & Short); Cic. Q. fr. 3.5: versūs (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    The plain everyday way to say it: versūs facere, poēma facere (Catull. 50.16, hoc, jūcunde, tibi poēma fēcī). For music, modōs facere (M-O s.v. compose (music), after Terence).

  • scrībō, scrībere, scrīpsī, scrīptum — write

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 409 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    “Write” in general (see write); with carmen or versūs it is “write a poem”.

Examples

  • hoc, jūcunde, tibi poēma fēcī

    I made this poem for you, my dear friendCatull. 50.16

  • sponte suā carmen numerōs veniēbat ad aptōs, et quod temptābam scrībere versus erat

    of its own accord my song fell into the right rhythm, and whatever I tried to write came out as verseOv. Tr. 4.10.25–26

See also poetry, poet, write.
